title: Chance-Constrained Optimal Path Planning With Obstacles
summary: Plans the future probability distribution of a linear-Gaussian vehicle so that the chance of collision or leaving the allowed region stays under a set bound. Bounds the collision probability so the problem becomes a disjunctive convex program, solved by branch-and-bound or a faster near-optimal method. IEEE T-RO 27(6), doi 10.1109/TRO.2011.2161160.
key_takeaways: The theory behind 'margin grows with position uncertainty'
Open-loop covariance, offline planning
Read from the abstract only

title: The Belief Roadmap: Efficient Planning in Belief Space by Factoring the Covariance
summary: Belief-space version of the probabilistic roadmap. Factoring the covariance turns several predict and update steps into one linear transfer, so covariance along roadmap edges is cheap to predict. Shown with UWB beacon localization, choosing routes that keep position accurate. IJRR 28(11-12), doi 10.1177/0278364909341659.
key_takeaways: Plans routes that keep localization good, not just short
Offline roadmap, linear-Gaussian assumption

title: Optimal Stochastic Vehicle Path Planning Using Covariance Steering
summary: Steers both mean and covariance of a linear stochastic system to a goal while obstacles are handled as non-convex chance constraints, using mixed-integer convex programming over a convex decomposition of free space. IEEE RA-L 2019.
key_takeaways: Closed-loop covariance gives less conservative paths than open-loop growth
Linear model, offline

title: Chance-Constrained Collision Avoidance for MAVs in Dynamic Environments
summary: Chance-constrained nonlinear MPC for quadrotors that keeps collision probability with each obstacle under a threshold, with a tight bound that makes it real-time. Uncertainty from localization, sensing and disturbances; real flights with two quadrotors and two people. IEEE RA-L 4(2):776-783.
key_takeaways: Live, onboard version of uncertainty-aware clearance for quadrotors
Strongest baseline for an uncertainty-inflated planner
Code is MATLAB, GPL-3.0

title: NanoMap: Fast, Uncertainty-Aware Proximity Queries with Lazy Search over Local 3D Data
summary: Skips global map fusion: keeps recent depth frames with noisy relative poses and answers proximity queries from the most certain view. The planner therefore sees pose uncertainty in obstacle distance. Quadrotor obstacle avoidance up to 10 m/s. ICRA 2018.
key_takeaways: Uncertainty-aware obstacle queries in the body frame
Cheap to apply loop-closure pose updates

title: Uncertainty-aware receding horizon exploration and mapping using aerial robots
summary: Two-step receding-horizon planner: a random tree finds branches that explore new space, then the branch that minimises expected localization uncertainty of a stereo visual-inertial system is flown. Verified on aerial robots in lit and dark conditions. ICRA 2017; journal version Auton. Robots 2019.
key_takeaways: Route choice driven by predicted VIO uncertainty
Exploration task, not A-to-B

title: Belief Control Barrier Functions for Risk-aware Control
summary: Peer-reviewed (IEEE RA-L 8(12):8565-8572, 2023, doi 10.1109/LRA.2023.3330662, confirmed via Crossref in docs/research/close-area-nav/05-cbf-baselines-faithful.md). Defines control barrier functions on the EKF belief (mean and covariance) so a controller keeps the robot in a safe set with a chosen confidence. The barrier uses the predicted covariance growth between updates and a margin for the jump at the next measurement update. Crazyflie hardware tests under varying sensing; control rates up to 1 kHz.
key_takeaways: Strongest prior art for clearance inflated by live covariance
Brakes before the margin grows: covariance prediction plus an update-jump margin (Theorem 3); a plain sqrt(lambda_max) inflation is a weaker copy
Gaussian belief only, faults not modelled

title: Integrity-Based Path Planning Strategy for Urban Autonomous Vehicular Navigation Using GPS and Cellular Signals
summary: Ground-vehicle path planner whose cost includes the predicted horizontal protection level along each candidate path, with a constraint that HPL stays under the alert limit. GPS and LTE pseudoranges are predicted by ray tracing over 3D city models, with multiple-fault handling. ION GNSS+ 2020, doi 10.33012/2020.17589.
key_takeaways: Uses a protection level, not a covariance, as the planning margin
Offline, ground vehicle, GNSS and cellular

title: Perception-aware Path Planning
summary: Online planner that scores paths by the photometric information a direct visual localizer would get, and replans as textured areas are discovered. Quadrotor demonstration. The authors' group lists it as T-RO 2016; venue not confirmed here.
key_takeaways: Original statement of perception-aware planning for VIO
Texture, not only geometry, decides a good path

title: Perception-aware trajectory generation for aggressive quadrotor flight using differential flatness
summary: Chooses a yaw trajectory that keeps tracked features co-visible while the position trajectory stays aggressive, using differential flatness. Reports almost 70% lower tracking RMSE thanks to better state estimation. ACC 2019.
key_takeaways: Yaw-only perception awareness is cheap and strong
The baseline any 48h perception-aware entry must beat

title: Perception-aware Path Planning for UAVs using Semantic Segmentation
summary: A* search plus B-spline optimisation that favours semantic classes known to be good for visual state estimation, with real-time replanning. Reports better state estimation than a reactive planner and than the Zhang-Scaramuzza perception-aware planner. IROS 2020.
key_takeaways: Semantic classes as a proxy for VIO quality
Later RL version at IROS 2021

title: RAPTOR: Robust and Perception-aware Trajectory Replanning for Quadrotor Fast Flight
summary: Fast replanning that searches several topological paths, refines for risk so obstacles are seen earlier, and plans yaw to look into unknown space. Aggressive indoor and outdoor flights. IEEE T-RO 37(6):1992-2009.
key_takeaways: Perception aimed at mapping unknown space, not at VIO health
Code lives in Fast-Planner (GPL-3.0)

title: Perception-Aware Time-Optimal Planning for Quadrotor Waypoint Flight
summary: Time-optimal trajectory optimisation with full dynamics, rotor limits, camera field-of-view constraints and an information-theoretic position-uncertainty metric, tracked by contouring MPC. Abstract reports real flights up to 9.8 m/s and Split-S success rising from 55% to 100%.
key_takeaways: Recent, strong perception-aware baseline for racing-style flight
Gate courses, not cluttered A-to-B

title: Embedded Safe Reactive Navigation for Multirotors Systems using Control Barrier Functions
summary: Composite control barrier function built only from onboard range measurements, inserted in the PX4 position and velocity loop as a minimal change to the acceleration setpoint. Does not need consistent localization or mapping. Accepted at ICUAS 2025 per the arXiv comment.
key_takeaways: Product-shaped safety filter already inside PX4
Strongest baseline for a close-area safety filter
Abstract gives no numbers

title: Control-Barrier-Aided Teleoperation with Visual-Inertial SLAM for Safe MAV Navigation in Complex Environments
summary: CBF safety filter on top of onboard VI-SLAM and dense occupancy mapping that corrects unsafe operator commands; unmapped space counts as unsafe. Real flights with onboard IMU, stereo infrared and depth only. ICRA 2024.
key_takeaways: Map-based safety filter on real VI-SLAM
Treats unknown space as unsafe
Does not react to estimator health

title: gatekeeper: Online Safety Verification and Control for Nonlinear Systems in Dynamic Environments
summary: Lightweight check between a planner and a controller: simulate the nominal trajectory to a switch time, then a backup controller such as hover, and commit the safe candidate with the latest switch time. Quadrotor hardware with an online map; 3-10x faster than MPC in simulation per the authors. Peer-reviewed: IEEE T-RO 40:4358-4375, 2024, doi 10.1109/TRO.2024.3454415, plus IROS 2023 pp. 259-266 (Crossref, per docs/research/close-area-nav/05-cbf-baselines-faithful.md).
key_takeaways: Planner-agnostic, easy to explain to judges
Needs a backup controller and backup set

title: Backup Control Barrier Functions: Formulation and Comparative Study
summary: General backup-CBF formulation: a fixed backup controller grows a small, easy control-invariant set into a larger one, and the filter keeps the system able to fall back to it. Compares backup CBFs with other safety methods.
key_takeaways: Turns a hover or brake controller into a safety filter
Arxiv checked; venue not confirmed

title: Onboard Safety Guarantees for Racing Drones: High-speed Geofencing with Control Barrier Functions
summary: Implicit CBF from a backup controller that avoids derivatives, cheap enough to run on a 10 g microcontroller. Geofences a 7-inch racing drone at over 100 km/h per the abstract.
key_takeaways: Geofence safety filter that fits on the flight controller
Backup-set CBF on full quadrotor dynamics needs more compute

title: A predictive safety filter for learning-based control of constrained nonlinear dynamical systems
summary: MPC-style filter that receives any proposed input, for example from an RL policy, and changes it only when needed to keep a safe backup plan feasible. Handles state- and input-dependent model uncertainty. Automatica 129, 2021, doi 10.1016/j.automatica.2021.109597.
key_takeaways: Theory for 'any planner plus a filter'
Heavier than a CBF-QP; needs an MPC solve

title: Guaranteeing Safety of Learned Perception Modules via Measurement-Robust Control Barrier Functions
summary: Measurement-robust CBFs choose safe inputs when the state comes from an uncertain, possibly learned, measurement model, and give a way to estimate how much perception error the controller tolerates. Simulated Segway. CoRL 2020, PMLR 155.
key_takeaways: Safety filter that accounts for state-estimate error
Not tested on a quadrotor

title: Measurement-Robust Control Barrier Functions: Certainty in Safety with Uncertainty in State
summary: Combines measurement-robust CBFs with the backup-set method to keep safety under imperfect state estimates. Simulation and a Segway with onboard stereo-camera state estimation. IROS 2021, doi 10.1109/IROS51168.2021.9636584.
key_takeaways: Bounded estimate error enters the barrier condition
Hardware result on a ground robot

title: Safe and Robust Observer-Controller Synthesis using Control Barrier Functions
summary: Builds CBFs from the bounded or input-to-state-stable error of the observer, giving QP controllers that stay safe from estimated states. Shows that a separately designed observer and controller can be unsafe. Quadrotor simulations and experiments. IEEE L-CSS 7:127-132.
key_takeaways: Design estimator and safety filter together
Quadrotor flight test where ignoring estimate error leads to collision (per search summary)

title: Closing the Loop on Runtime Monitors with Fallback-Safe MPC
summary: Robust MPC that uses perception estimates while keeping a fallback plan that does not depend on perception, paired with a runtime monitor calibrated by conformal prediction. When the monitor fires, the fallback runs. Aircraft taxiing sim and a simulated quadrotor that slows and descends. CDC 2023.
key_takeaways: Monitor => slow down, with a calibrated alarm
Perception errors were simulated

title: Robust Safety under Stochastic Uncertainty with Discrete-Time Control Barrier Functions
summary: Finite-time safety bounds, from martingale theory, for discrete-time CBF controllers under unbounded stochastic disturbances such as estimation noise. RSS 2023.
key_takeaways: Gives a probability of staying safe over a horizon, not a hard guarantee
Theory for the noisy-estimate case

title: Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance for Quadrotors with Event Cameras
summary: Uses event timing to split moving from static objects and commands a dodge, with about 3.5 ms latency, against objects at relative speeds up to 10 m/s, onboard only. Science Robotics 5(40), doi 10.1126/scirobotics.aaz9712.
key_takeaways: Latency is the limit for dynamic obstacles
Needs event-camera hardware

title: Automatic Re-Initialization and Failure Recovery for Aggressive Flight with a Monocular Vision-Based Quadrotor
summary: After visual tracking is lost or the vehicle is thrown, it stabilises attitude and height from IMU and a range sensor, then re-initialises the monocular visual pipeline before resuming. ICRA 2015.
key_takeaways: The standard answer to VIO loss: stabilise, then re-initialise
No multi-hypothesis relocalization
